lines.trans: Morning, everyone! Ernesto told me at the gate that you dug up buried treasure!
Better than gold coins, Tomas—look at this cream kitchen card from the tin!
Summer Berry and Almond Courtyard Cake—written in neat blue fountain pen!
Two hundred grams of ground almonds, soft butter, three eggs, and fresh summer berries...
Why did you stop reading at the best part, Rocio?
Because someone tore the recipe card cleanly in half right across the middle!
Turn the half card over, my dear—there is a pencilled note on the back.

words.gloss: give it (dale la vuelta = turn it over)

lines.trans: Read it aloud, Rocio! Where did they hide the baking time and the glaze?
Half in the tin, half pressed inside our favourite green book of garden leaves!
A recipe split into two halves like a treasure map—who bakes like that?!
Two clever friends who wanted us to search both the courtyard and the bookshelves!
Until we find that green leaf book, nobody gets a single slice of berry cake!

Half in the tin, half pressed inside our favourite green book of garden leaves!

lines.trans: Read it aloud, Rocio! Where did they hide the baking time and the glaze?
Half in the tin, half pressed inside our favourite green book of garden leaves!
A recipe split into two halves like a treasure map—who bakes like that?!
Two clever friends who wanted us to search both the courtyard and the bookshelves!
Until we find that green leaf book, nobody gets a single slice of berry cake!
See you soon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.text: Vamos a la estación ahora.
examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.

examples.text: ¿Hay alguien en recepción?
examples.trans: Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Classic Mediterranean baking ingredient in tarts and biscuits.

examples.text: Rocío hornea galletas crujientes de almendra y limón.
examples.trans: Rocio bakes crunchy almond and lemon biscuits.

examples.text: Tostamos las almendras cinco minutos en el horno.
examples.trans: We toast the almonds for five minutes in the oven.

meanings.note: Alto y claro means 'loud and clear'.

examples.text: Es una pieza alta.
examples.trans: It is a tall piece.

examples.text: Alto y claro. ¿Estás junto a la fuentecita de piedra?
examples.trans: Loud and clear. Are you beside the little stone fountain?

meanings.note: Feminine: la amiga.

examples.text: El amigo está aquí.
examples.trans: The friend is here.

examples.text: Vemos los amigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the friends from the door.

meanings.note: Así que means 'so / therefore'.

examples.text: Hazlo así, despacio.
examples.trans: Do it like this, slowly.

examples.text: Llueve mucho, así que entramos.
examples.trans: It is raining hard, so let us go inside.

meanings.note: Plural azules; azul marino means 'navy blue'.

examples.text: Es una pieza azul.
examples.trans: It is a blue piece.

examples.text: Espere, ¡es azul oscuro, igual que la suya!
examples.trans: Wait, it is dark blue, just like yours!

meanings.note: Commonly masculine (sin azúcar = without sugar).

examples.text: El azúcar es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sugar is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el azúcar.
examples.trans: We talk about the sugar.

meanings.note: Tall, light home-baked cake popular for breakfast or afternoon merienda in Spain.

examples.text: El bizcocho está aquí.
examples.trans: The sponge cake is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bizcochos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sponge cakes from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of duro (hard).

examples.text: Es una pieza blanda.
examples.trans: It is a soft piece.

examples.text: ¡Y yo tengo dos almohadas blandas y una alfombra azul en el almacén!
examples.trans: And I have two soft pillows and a blue rug in the storeroom!

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.text: ¡Buenos días a todos!
examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!

examples.text: Hace muy buen tiempo hoy.
examples.trans: The weather is very nice today.

buscar.gloss: to look for; to search for

meanings.en: to look for; to search for
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'for' (busco la llave = I am looking for the key).

examples.text: Busco la puerta azul.
examples.trans: I am looking for the blue door.

examples.text: Ayer busqué mis gafas por toda la casa.
examples.trans: Yesterday I looked for my glasses all over the house.

meanings.note: Coger cariño a = to grow fond of; also a warm term of endearment in Spain.

examples.text: El cariño es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The affection is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre el cariño.
examples.trans: We talk about the affection.

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.text: La cocina está aquí.
examples.trans: The kitchen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cocinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the kitchens from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented como compares or gives a reason (distinct from interrogative cómo).

examples.text: Está fría como el agua del río.
examples.trans: It is as cold as river water.

examples.text: Todo funciona como debe ser.
examples.trans: Everything works just as it should.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.text: Tomo café con leche caliente.
examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.

examples.text: Habla con calma, por favor.
examples.trans: Speak calmly, please.

dar.gloss: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)

meanings.en: to give; to face onto (dar a); to strike (the hour)
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg doy and preterite di/dio; dar las doce = strike twelve.

examples.text: La ventana da al patio soleado.
examples.trans: The window looks out onto the sunny courtyard.

examples.text: El reloj acaba de dar las doce.
examples.trans: The clock has just struck twelve.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Querer decir means 'to mean'.

examples.text: ¿Qué dice la carta exactamente?
examples.trans: What does the letter say exactly?

examples.text: Dime la verdad sin miedo.
examples.trans: Tell me the truth without fear.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.

examples.text: Déjame ayudarte con esa caja.
examples.trans: Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Soy vecino del barrio.
examples.trans: I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Dentro de + time means 'in (after) a certain amount of time'.

examples.text: Hay cuatro mesas dentro.
examples.trans: There are four tables inside.

examples.text: Vuelvo dentro de diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will be back in ten minutes.

meanings.note: Detrás de + noun means 'behind something'.

examples.text: El jardín está detrás de la casa.
examples.trans: The garden is behind the house.

examples.text: Hay otra página detrás del aviso.
examples.trans: There is another page behind the notice.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender with the plural noun that follows: doscientos gramos (masculine) vs. doscientas páginas (feminine).

examples.text: La receta pide doscientos gramos de almendra molida.
examples.trans: The recipe calls for two hundred grams of ground almonds.

examples.text: El edificio antiguo tiene más de doscientos años.
examples.trans: The old building is more than two hundred years old.

meanings.note: Masculine despite ending in -a: el día, ¡Buenos días!.

examples.text: El día está aquí.
examples.trans: The day is here.

examples.text: Vemos los días desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the days from the door.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb with written accent.

examples.text: Mira dónde señala con el lápiz.
examples.trans: Look where he is pointing with his pencil.

examples.text: ¿Dónde van las cucharillas y las servilletas?
examples.trans: Where do the teaspoons and the napkins go?

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.text: El patio tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.

examples.text: Pásame el libro de reservas.
examples.trans: Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: encuentro).

examples.text: No encuentro mis gafas de leer.
examples.trans: I cannot find my reading glasses.

examples.text: Encontramos una panadería estupenda.
examples.trans: We found a terrific bakery.

meanings.note: Esconderse detrás de = to hide behind.

examples.text: Escondo el regalo en el armario.
examples.trans: I hide the present in the wardrobe.

examples.text: El gato se escondió detrás de la maceta.
examples.trans: The cat hid behind the flowerpot.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb with irregular past participle escrito.

examples.text: Escribo la nota con lápiz azul.
examples.trans: I write the note in blue pencil.

examples.text: Mi hermano me escribió una postal corta.
examples.trans: My brother wrote me a short postcard.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.text: Pásame ese cuaderno azul.
examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Wooden wall or cupboard shelf.

examples.text: El estante está aquí.
examples.trans: The shelf is here.

examples.text: Vemos los estantes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the shelves from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.text: Este patio es muy tranquilo.
examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.

examples.text: Esta mañana hace mucho sol.
examples.trans: This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with its noun.

examples.text: Es una pieza favorita.
examples.trans: It is a favourite piece.

examples.text: ¡Solo vestidos, partituras y mi taza favorita!
examples.trans: Only dresses, sheet music, and my favourite cup!

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el final), means the ending of a song, book, or day.

examples.text: El final del vals baja el ritmo poco a poco.
examples.trans: The ending of the waltz slows the tempo little by little.

examples.text: Al final de la tarde probamos las dos sopas.
examples.trans: At the end of the afternoon we tasted both soups.

meanings.note: Pintura fresca = wet paint; agua fresca = cool water.

examples.text: Es una pieza fresca.
examples.trans: It is a cool piece.

examples.text: Bien. Pon estas hierbas frescas por encima antes de servirlos.
examples.trans: Good. Put these fresh herbs on top before serving them.

meanings.note: While la fruta is everyday table fruit, masculine el fruto appears in culinary groupings like frutos rojos ('red summer berries') and frutos secos ('nuts and dried fruit').

examples.text: Horneamos un bizcocho de almendra y frutos rojos.
examples.trans: We baked an almond and summer berry sponge cake.

examples.text: El limonero da sus mejores frutos en primavera.
examples.trans: The lemon tree bears its finest fruit in spring.

meanings.note: Standard metric weight unit in Spanish kitchen recipes (cien gramos de harina, doscientos gramos de almendra).

examples.text: Pesa doscientos gramos de almendra molida en la báscula.
examples.trans: Weigh out two hundred grams of ground almonds on the scale.

examples.text: Añade cincuenta gramos de azúcar al final.
examples.trans: Add fifty grams of sugar at the end.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.

examples.text: Ya hemos preparado las habitaciones.
examples.trans: We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Sigue recto hasta el puente.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.

examples.text: Nos quedamos hasta el viernes.
examples.trans: We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Means both a tree leaf and a single sheet of paper.

examples.text: La hoja está aquí.
examples.trans: The leaf is here.

examples.text: Vemos las hojas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the leaves from the door.

meanings.note: Del horno = out of the oven.

examples.text: El horno está aquí.
examples.trans: The oven is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hornos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the ovens from the door.

meanings.note: Huevos revueltos = scrambled eggs.

examples.text: El huevo está aquí.
examples.trans: The egg is here.

examples.text: Vemos los huevos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the eggs from the door.

meanings.note: Describes both a quick-thinking person (un amigo ingenioso) and a clever design or puzzle (una idea ingeniosa).

examples.text: Dos amigos ingeniosos partieron la receta en dos mitades.
examples.trans: Two clever friends split the recipe into two halves.

examples.text: El carpintero encontró una solución muy ingeniosa.
examples.trans: The carpenter found a very ingenious solution.

meanings.note: Plural jardines, without the written accent.

examples.text: Mi madre tiene flores en el jardín.
examples.trans: My mother has flowers in the garden.

examples.text: Los niños juegan en el jardín.
examples.trans: The children play in the garden.

meanings.note: Justo aquí = right here; justo al lado = right next door.

examples.text: La llave está justo aquí.
examples.trans: The key is right here.

examples.text: La panadería queda justo al lado.
examples.trans: The bakery is right next door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.

examples.text: La habitación tiene mucha luz.
examples.trans: The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: De lata means 'made of tin / tinplate' (una caja de lata); una lata also means a food can.

examples.text: Mi abuela guardaba los botones en una caja redonda de lata.
examples.trans: My grandmother kept buttons in a round tin box.

examples.text: Abrimos una lata de aceitunas para el aperitivo.
examples.trans: We opened a tin of olives for the snack.

meanings.note: Preterite 3rd sg/pl spells y: leyó, leyeron; past participle leído.

examples.text: Leo el periódico con el primer café.
examples.trans: I read the newspaper with my first coffee.

examples.text: Anoche leímos toda la carta juntos.
examples.trans: Last night we read the whole letter together.

meanings.note: Libro de reservas = reservation ledger.

examples.text: El libro está aquí.
examples.trans: The book is here.

examples.text: Vemos los libros desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the books from the door.

meanings.note: Opposite of sucio (dirty).

examples.text: Es una pieza limpia.
examples.trans: It is a clean piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene un paño limpio y agua fría, Ernesto.
examples.trans: Here is a clean cloth and cold water, Ernesto.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.text: Los vecinos vienen a desayunar.
examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Plural los lápices; a lápiz = in pencil.

examples.text: El lápiz está aquí.
examples.trans: The pencil is here.

examples.text: Vemos los lápices desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pencils from the door.

meanings.note: Spread on warm morning toast.

examples.text: La mantequilla es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The butter is very important here.

examples.text: Hablamos sobre la mantequilla.
examples.trans: We talk about the butter.

meanings.note: Masculine noun despite ending in -a: el mapa antiguo, estos mapas mojados.

examples.text: Mateo dibujó un mapa sencillo para llegar a la ferretería.
examples.trans: Mateo drew a simple map to get to the hardware shop.

examples.text: Extendimos el mapa de Valencia sobre la mesa de madera.
examples.trans: We spread the map of Valencia out on the wooden table.

meanings.note: First-person singular object/reflexive pronoun.

examples.text: ¿Me pasas la sal, por favor?
examples.trans: Can you pass me the salt, please?

examples.text: Vivo aquí y trabajo aquí.
examples.trans: I live here and I work here.

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.text: Es una pieza media.
examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative/superlative of bueno; plural mejores.

examples.text: Esta ventana tiene la mejor vista.
examples.trans: This window has the best view.

examples.text: Hoy el radiador calienta mejor.
examples.trans: Today the radiator heats better.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: A mitad de precio = at half price.

examples.text: La mitad está aquí.
examples.trans: The half is here.

examples.text: Vemos las mitades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the halves from the door.

meanings.note: Past participle of moler ('to grind') used as a culinary adjective: almendra molida ('ground almonds'), café molido ('ground coffee').

examples.text: Mezcla doscientos gramos de almendra molida con mantequilla.
examples.trans: Mix two hundred grams of ground almonds with butter.

examples.text: Me encanta el aroma del café recién molido por la mañana.
examples.trans: I love the aroma of freshly ground coffee in the morning.

meanings.note: Metal coin.

examples.text: La moneda está aquí.
examples.trans: The coin is here.

examples.text: Vemos las monedas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coins from the door.

meanings.note: Shortened form of mucho used before adjectives and adverbs.

examples.text: El bizcocho está muy rico.
examples.trans: The sponge cake is very tasty.

examples.text: Camina muy rápido por el puente.
examples.trans: She walks very fast across the bridge.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.

examples.text: Nadie conoce mejor este edificio.
examples.trans: Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Ni... ni... = neither... nor...; ni una gota = not a single drop.

examples.text: No cae ni una sola gota.
examples.trans: Not a single drop is falling.

examples.text: No tengo ni papel ni bolígrafo.
examples.trans: I have neither paper nor pen.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.text: Hoy no llueve en Valencia.
examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

meanings.note: Covers jotted notes, musical notes, and review scores.

examples.text: La nota está aquí.
examples.trans: The note is here.

examples.text: Vemos las notas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the notes from the door.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.text: Nuestra posada tiene ocho habitaciones.
examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.

examples.text: Nuestros vecinos toman café aquí.
examples.trans: Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.en: gold (precious metal, color, or something of great value)
meanings.note: Masculine noun. Frequently used figuratively in the idiom 'valer oro' ('to be worth its weight in gold / to be priceless'), as when Paquita savors the fresh country air of her hometown.

meanings.en: oros (suit of golden coins in the Spanish card deck)
meanings.note: In the plural ('los oros'), refers to the suit of coins in the traditional Spanish deck of cards ('la baraja española').

examples.text: Este aire... (ASPIRA) Este aire vale oro.
examples.trans: This air... (INHALES) This air is worth its weight in gold.

examples.text: Esa representante tiene un corazón de oro aunque a veces pierda los nervios.
examples.trans: That talent agent has a heart of gold even though she loses her temper sometimes.

meanings.note: Spanish never puts un/una before otro (otra taza = another cup; otra vez = again).

examples.text: ¿Quiere otra taza de café?
examples.trans: Would you like another cup of coffee?

examples.text: Míralo otra vez a la luz.
examples.trans: Look at it again in the light.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la mejor parte.

examples.text: La parte está aquí.
examples.trans: The part is here.

examples.text: Vemos las partes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parts from the door.

partir.gloss: to split; to cut; to divide; to depart

meanings.en: to split; to cut; to divide; to depart
meanings.note: Partir por la mitad is the everyday Spanish phrase for tearing, cutting, or splitting something cleanly in half.

examples.text: Alguien partió la tarjeta de la receta por la mitad.
examples.trans: Someone tore the recipe card in half.

examples.text: Rocío partió el bizcocho caliente en ocho trozos iguales.
examples.trans: Rocío cut the warm sponge cake into eight equal slices.

meanings.note: Traditional inner courtyard at the heart of a Spanish building.

examples.text: El patio está aquí.
examples.trans: The courtyard is here.

examples.text: Vemos los patios desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the courtyards from the door.

meanings.note: In Spanish LGBTQ+ and colloquial usage, 'tener pluma' or 'subirse de pluma' refers to noticeably campy or effeminate mannerisms.
Literal sense of the feminine noun 'la pluma'.

examples.text: pero se les sube de pluma, no... Sí.
examples.trans: but they get a bit too campy, right... Yes.

examples.text: Que se les sube mucho de pluma, dicen.
examples.trans: They say their campiness really comes out.

related.gloss: feather duster (in 'ver el plumero' = see someone's true colors)

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.text: Paseamos por el casco antiguo.
examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: One word without accent (distinct from ¿por qué? = why?).

examples.text: Abro la ventana porque hace calor.
examples.trans: I open the window because it is warm.

examples.text: Sonríe porque huele a canela.
examples.trans: She smiles because it smells of cinnamon.

probar.gloss: to try; to taste; to test

meanings.en: to try; to taste; to test
meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: pruebo).

examples.text: Prueba este pan con aceite de oliva.
examples.trans: Try this bread with olive oil.

examples.text: Ayer probamos la mermelada de manzana.
examples.trans: Yesterday we tasted the apple jam.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.text: ¡Hasta pronto y buen viaje!
examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Covers room doors, street doors, and courtyard gates.

examples.text: La puerta está aquí.
examples.trans: The door is here.

examples.text: Vemos las puertas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doors from the door.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.text: Espero que descanses muy bien.
examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.text: ¿Quiere usted café o té caliente?
examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?

examples.text: Lo abrí sin querer.
examples.trans: I opened it by accident.

meanings.note: Plural quiénes; ¿de quién es? = whose is it?

examples.text: ¿Quién ha dejado este sobre aquí?
examples.trans: Who left this envelope here?

examples.text: ¿De quién es esta maleta azul?
examples.trans: Whose blue suitcase is this?

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.text: ¿Qué hora es ahora mismo?
examples.trans: What time is it right now?

examples.text: ¡Qué mañana tan luminosa!
examples.trans: What a bright morning!

meanings.note: In the kitchen, una receta (de cocina) is a recipe; at a pharmacy or doctor's surgery, it means a prescription.

examples.text: Encontramos la mitad de una receta de bizcocho de almendra.
examples.trans: We found half of an almond sponge cake recipe.

examples.text: Esta sopa sigue una receta antigua de mi abuela.
examples.trans: This soup follows an old recipe of my grandmother's.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number.

examples.text: Es una pieza roja.
examples.trans: It is a red piece.

examples.text: ¡Dígales que la mía tiene una cinta roja en el bolsillo de arriba!
examples.trans: Tell them mine has a red ribbon in the top pocket!

sacar.gloss: to take out; to pull out

meanings.en: to take out; to pull out
meanings.note: Spelling changes c -> qu before -e (saqué).

examples.text: Rocío acaba de sacar el pan caliente del horno.
examples.trans: Rocio just took the hot bread out of the oven.

examples.text: Saca las llaves pequeñas del bolsillo del abrigo.
examples.trans: Take the small keys out of your coat pocket.

salir.gloss: to go out; to come out; to leave

meanings.en: to go out; to come out; to leave
meanings.note: Irregular 1st sg salgo; salir corriendo = run out.

examples.text: El pan acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The bread just came out of the oven.

examples.text: Salgo temprano hacia la estación.
examples.trans: I leave early for the station.

meanings.note: After a verb, invariable tanto means 'so much' (¿por qué mira tanto?).

examples.text: ¿Cómo recuerdas eso después de tantos años?
examples.trans: How do you remember that after so many years?

examples.text: Gracias por tener tanta paciencia.
examples.trans: Thank you for having so much patience.

meanings.note: Pagar con tarjeta = pay by card.

examples.text: La tarjeta está aquí.
examples.trans: The card is here.

examples.text: Vemos las tarjetas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cards from the door.

meanings.note: Appears in un mapa del tesoro ('a treasure map') and buscadores de tesoros ('treasure hunters').

examples.text: Ernesto dijo que habéis sacado un tesoro bajo las piedras.
examples.trans: Ernesto said that you dug up a treasure under the stones.

examples.text: La receta partida parece un auténtico mapa del tesoro.
examples.trans: The split recipe looks like a real treasure map.

meanings.note: ¿Qué tiempo hace? asks about the weather; a tiempo = on time.

examples.text: El tiempo está aquí.
examples.trans: The time is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tiempos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the times from the door.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.text: Ponemos tres mesas bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We set three tables under the tree.

examples.text: Empieza con tres frases cortas.
examples.trans: Start with three short sentences.

meanings.note: Un trozo de bizcocho = a piece of cake.

examples.text: El trozo está aquí.
examples.trans: The piece is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trozos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the pieces from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Same form for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: Es una pieza verde.
examples.trans: It is a green piece.

examples.text: Mateo, ¿me oyes? ¡Acabo de pasar la farmacia verde!
examples.trans: Mateo, can you hear me? I just passed the green pharmacy!

meanings.note: Plural las voces; en voz baja = in a low voice.

examples.text: La voz está aquí.
examples.trans: The voice is here.

examples.text: Vemos las voces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the voices from the door.

vuelta.gloss: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)

meanings.en: turn; return (de vuelta = back; media vuelta = turn around)
meanings.note: Dar una vuelta = take a stroll / make one turn.

examples.text: La vuelta está aquí.
examples.trans: The turn is here.

examples.text: Vemos las vueltas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the turns from the door.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.

examples.text: Son las siete y cuarto.
examples.trans: It is quarter past seven.
